schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE badges
(
    Id     INTEGER          not null
        primary key,
    UserId INTEGER          null,
    Name   TEXT null,
    Date   DATETIME     null,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE comments
(
    Id              INTEGER          not null
        primary key,
    PostId          INTEGER          null,
    Score           INTEGER          null,
    Text            TEXT     null,
    CreationDate    DATETIME     null,
    UserId          INTEGER          null,
    UserDisplayName TEXT null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE postHistory
(
    Id                INTEGER          not null UNIQUE
        primary key,
    PostHistoryTypeId INTEGER          null,
    PostId            INTEGER          null,
    RevisionGUID      TEXT null,
    CreationDate      DATETIME     null,
    UserId            INTEGER          null,
    Text              TEXT     null,
    Comment           TEXT         null,
    UserDisplayName   TEXT null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE postLinks
(
    Id            INTEGER      not null
        primary key,
    CreationDate  DATETIME null,
    PostId        INTEGER      null,
    RelatedPostId INTEGER      null,
    LinkTypeId    INTEGER      null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (RelatedPostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE posts
(
    Id                    INTEGER          not null UNIQUE
        primary key,
    PostTypeId            INTEGER          null,
    AcceptedAnswerId      INTEGER          null,
    CreaionDate           DATETIME     null,
    Score                 INTEGER          null,
    ViewCount             INTEGER          null,
    Body                  TEXT     null,
    OwnerUserId           INTEGER          null,
    LasActivityDate       DATETIME     null,
    Title                 TEXT null,
    Tags                  TEXT null,
    AnswerCount           INTEGER          null,
    CommentCount          INTEGER          null,
    FavoriteCount         INTEGER          null,
    LastEditorUserId      INTEGER          null,
    LastEditDate          DATETIME     null,
    CommunityOwnedDate    DATETIME    null,
    ParentId              INTEGER          null,
    ClosedDate            DATETIME     null,
    OwnerDisplayName      TEXT null,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT null,
        foreign key (LastEditorUserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (OwnerUserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE tags
(
    Id            INTEGER          not null
        primary key,
    TagName       TEXT null,
    Count         INTEGER          null,
    ExcerptPostId INTEGER          null,
    WikiPostId    INTEGER          null,
    foreign key (ExcerptPostId) references posts (Id)
        on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE users
(
    Id              INTEGER          not null UNIQUE
        primary key,
    Reputation      INTEGER          null,
    CreationDate    DATETIME     null,
    DisplayName     TEXT null,
    LastAccessDate  DATETIME     null,
    WebsiteUrl      TEXT null,
    Location        TEXT null,
    AboutMe         TEXT     null,
    Views           INTEGER          null,
    UpVotes         INTEGER          null,
    DownVotes       INTEGER          null,
    AccountId       INTEGER          null,
    Age             INTEGER          null,
    ProfileImageUrl TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE votes
(
    Id           INTEGER  not null
        primary key,
    PostId       INTEGER  null,
    VoteTypeId   INTEGER  null,
    CreationDate DATE null,
    UserId       INTEGER  null,
    BountyAmount INTEGER  null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

explanation: Q1 divides the count of badges by the count of distinct user display names (users.DisplayName), while Q2 divides by the count of distinct user IDs (badges.UserId). If two users share the same DisplayName but have distinct IDs, Q1's denominator will be smaller than Q2's, leading to different results.
counterexample_dsp: Two users with the same DisplayName and Views > 200 each have one badge. Q1's denominator counts 1 distinct DisplayName, while Q2's counts 2 distinct UserIds, producing different division results.

Okay, let's tackle this problem. So, I need to find a counterexample where Q1 and Q2 give different results. Let me first understand what each query is doing.

Looking at Q1: It selects the count of T1.Id (which is badges.Id) divided by the count of distinct T2.DisplayName (users.DisplayName) from badges joined with users on UserId = Id, where T2.Views > 200. So the denominator is the number of distinct user display names that meet the view condition.

Q2: It does a similar division but the denominator is COUNT(DISTINCT T1.UserId). So instead of counting distinct display names from users, it's counting distinct user IDs from the badges table.

Wait, the join is on badges.UserId = users.Id. So T1 is badges, T2 is users. So in Q1, COUNT(DISTINCT T2.DisplayName) would count distinct user display names from the users table for all the joined rows where T2.Views > 200. In Q2, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.UserId) counts distinct user IDs from the badges table for those same rows.

But why would these be different? Because the users table might have duplicate display names for different users. For example, if two different users have the same DisplayName, then COUNT(DISTINCT DisplayName) would be 1 for those two, while COUNT(DISTINCT UserId) would be 2. However, in the join, each row in badges is linked to one user. But if the same user has multiple badges, then T1.UserId would be the same, so COUNT(DISTINCT T1.UserId) would count unique users.

Wait, but the join is inner join between badges and users on UserId = Id. So for each badge row, there's a user row. The WHERE condition is T2.Views > 200, which filters users with more than 200 views.

So, the denominator in Q1 is the number of distinct users (by DisplayName) that have views > 200, but since DisplayName isn't unique, if two users have the same DisplayName, they would count as one in Q1's denominator. In Q2, the denominator is the count of distinct UserIds from badges, which would be the number of unique users who have badges and meet the view condition. Wait, no: in Q2, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.UserId) counts distinct user IDs from the badges table. But since each badge row has a UserId, if a user has multiple badges, they would still count once. So in that case, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.UserId) is the number of unique users who have at least one badge in the joined set (with views > 200). But COUNT(DISTINCT T2.DisplayName) in Q1 is the number of unique display names among those same users.

So the difference arises when two different users have the same DisplayName. For example, if two different users have the same DisplayName and both have views > 200, then Q1's denominator would count 1, while Q2's denominator would count 2 (since each user is distinct by their UserId). Therefore, the division would yield different results.

So to create a counterexample, I need two users with the same DisplayName, both having Views > 200. Then, each of them should have at least one badge. Then, the count of badges (numerator) divided by COUNT(DISTINCT DisplayName) (which is 1) would be different from dividing by COUNT(DISTINCT UserId) (which is 2).

Let me structure that. Let's say there are two users: User1 (Id=1, DisplayName='John', Views=300) and User2 (Id=2, DisplayName='John', Views=300). Each has one badge. Then:

Q1's denominator is COUNT(DISTINCT T2.DisplayName) = 1 (since both have same display name).

Q2's denominator is COUNT(DISTINCT T1.UserId) = 2 (two distinct user IDs).

The numerator in both is COUNT(T1.Id) = 2 (two badges). So Q1 would be 2/1 = 2.0, Q2 would be 2/2 = 1.0. Different results.

That's a valid counterexample. Now, I need to create this in the database schema. Let's insert the users and badges accordingly.

Also, need to make sure that the views are above 200. Let me check the users table: the Views column is an integer. So inserting two users with Views=300 each.

Then, insert two badges, each with UserId=1 and UserId=2 respectively.
